chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a people worshipped Allah alone, with no partner for Him, and established the prayer, and gave the alms-tax, and performed the pilgrimage to the House, and fasted the month of Ramadan, then they said regarding something that Allah or the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did,
Why was it not done differently than what was done,
or they found that in their hearts,
then they would be polytheists because of that.'

So no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge of that over which they dispute among themselves, then they will not find in their hearts any discomfort from what you judged and they will submit with [full] submission.
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So upon you is submission.'

key_terms.مُشْرِكِينَ: Polytheists (those who associate partners with God)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between outward worship and true belief according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that ritual correctness alone does not guarantee monotheism; true faith requires 'taslim' (unconditional submission) where the heart feels no inner reservation regarding Divine or Prophetic decrees. By citing Quran :65, he links the external act of worship to the internal state of the heart, establishing that doubt in the wisdom of God's actions constitutes a form of shirk. This hadith is foundational in Shia theology for distinguishing between mere ritualism and genuine, heartfelt acceptance of authority.
